audit.whatIsWrong: The chart read Cassiopeia/Skill/Skill/Skill/Skill/Ryze/Ryze in both layers while every why underneath argues the opposite: whys[1] through whys[5] all describe Cassiopeia winning, and only whys[6] gives Ryze the edge.
audit.why: The packet levelChart reads Skill/Cassiopeia x5/Ryze, matching the prose. Level 1 is genuinely contested — Overload throws 1000 against her 850 Noxious Blast — but from level 2 onward her poison-into-Twin-Fang loop and Miasma's ground own every stage until Ryze's second item.
audit.corrected: All seven rows aligned to the packet in both layers as matched pairs, ratings moved with them, and the four templated phase whys that then argued the wrong side rewritten.

audit.whatIsWrong: spikes[1] contains the duplicated phrase "Realm Warp's channel channel" and builds the level 3-5 spike on Miasma cancelling Realm Warp.
audit.why: Realm Warp is not a channel — it creates a portal that fires after a delay. Whether Grounded prevents casting it is not answerable from Riot's text, and the mirror (cassiopeia__ryze) deliberately narrowed the same claim to Flash rather than assert it. What is certain: Miasma grounds, is 24s at rank 1, and Ryze has no dash, so the ground's real cost to him is Flash and the step-back.
audit.corrected: Spike rebuilt on Miasma's 24s rank-1 cooldown and the loss of Flash, with the cancel claim removed rather than restated.

audit.whatIsWrong: whys[3] states Twin Fang "costs zero mana on a poisoned target" and spikes[2] says it "refunds cooldowns". whys[0] and early both say Ryze must walk to melee range to trade. Twin Fang's healing is never mentioned as the reason short trades fail.
audit.why: Twin Fang costs 40 mana at every rank and fires on a 0.75s cooldown at 700 range; Riot's text grants mana back only when the target dies from it, and says nothing about cooldown refunds. It also heals her for a percentage of the damage dealt — that heal, not a mana quirk, is what beats Ryze's chip. Overload is 1000 range and Spell Flux 615, so nothing here happens at melee range.
audit.corrected: Real cost, cadence and heal stated; the mana and cooldown-refund inventions removed; ranges corrected to 1000 and 615 against her 850 and 700.

edits.before: At level 1 you only have Q, which means walking into melee range to trade — Cassiopeia punishes this instantly with Noxious Blast (Q) poison into Twin Fang spam that refunds its own cooldown. Do not fight. Last-hit with Q at its max range and accept that she controls the wave. At level 2 your W root gives you one real threat: if she overextends to push, root her before she can drop Miasma and squeeze off empowered Q. Level 3 completes your E-Q-W loop, but she completes hers too — the key is that your W root must land BEFORE her W Miasma hits the ground, or you are grounded and your entire damage window collapses. Bait her into stepping onto your E Flux mark by feinting forward, then immediately chain W-Q.
edits.after: At level 1 Overload actually outranges her — 1000 against her 850 — but Spell Flux needs 615 and that walk is what Noxious Blast punishes, because the poison turns on a 0.75s Twin Fang that heals her back. Do not fight. Last-hit from max Q range and accept she controls the wave. At level 2 your root is a threat only against a Fluxed target: if she overextends, Flux her first, then Rune Prison, then Q. Level 3 completes your loop and hers — the whole lane is whether Flux-then-root lands before Miasma hits the ground, because grounded you lose Flash and the step-back. Feint forward, make her commit the pool, then chain.

edits.before: Levels 4-6 are a slow, careful farm phase — her Twin Fang costs no mana when a target is poisoned, so she can infinitely pressure while your mana bar bleeds pre-Seraph's. Stay at the range where your Q can tag the minion wave's back rank and do not step forward unless her Q is visibly on cooldown. Her Miasma also blocks your Realm Warp channel, so at level 6 she can deny your roam simply by throwing W at your feet when she sees the cast animation — factor this into any warp plan and pre-move away from her before channeling.
edits.after: Levels 4-6 are a slow, careful farm phase — Twin Fang costs her only 40 a cast and heals her off the poison, so she pressures indefinitely while your mana bleeds pre-Seraph's. Stay where Overload's 1000 tags the back rank and step forward only when Noxious Blast is visibly down on its 3.5s. At 6 she gains Petrifying Gaze, which stuns from 825 anyone facing her — turn and walk before it lands rather than trading into it, and place any Realm Warp well away from her Miasma range so the ground never catches you standing on the portal.

edits.before: Drop Miasma (W) on your feet the moment you step up, grounding your dash and blocking your Realm Warp channel
edits.after: Drop Miasma on your feet the moment you step up — the ground takes your Flash and kills the step-back

notes: The packet suspectName 'Realm Warp's' is a false positive on the name but sat on a real defect: spikes[1] read 'Realm Warp's channel channel' and asserted Miasma cancels it. Realm Warp is a delayed portal, not a channel, and — following the mirror's reasoning — whether Grounded blocks casting it is not answerable from Riot's text, so I removed the claim instead of restating it and kept only the verifiable cost of being grounded (no Flash). Also killed the 'Twin Fang costs zero mana on a poisoned target' and 'Twin Fang refunds cooldowns' claims: it costs 40 at every rank on a flat 0.75s, and Riot's text refunds mana only on a kill. The whole chart was flipped to the packet ordering, which the page's own whys already described; the mirror recorded no chart change, so cassiopeia__ryze should be re-checked for the inverse.
